1: The Preacher looks at life "under the sun": generations come and go, and nothing is new. Even wisdom brings sorrow.
The book asks what anything is worth if this life is all there is.
2: He tries pleasure, building, wealth and wisdom. All is vanity, because wise and fool both die. Enjoy your work as God's gift.
Nothing created can fill the heart.
3: "A time to be born and a time to die." God has made everything beautiful in its time and put eternity into man's heart.
We are made for more than time can give.
4: He sees oppression, envy and lonely toil. "A threefold cord is not quickly broken."
Companionship is one of life's real goods.
5: Guard your steps in God's house, and keep your vows. Whoever loves money never has enough.
Reverence in worship; contentment with what God gives.
6: A man may have everything and not be able to enjoy it.
The power to enjoy is itself a gift from God.
7: Better the house of mourning than the house of feasting. Do not ask why former days were better. God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes.
Thinking about death makes us wise.
8: Obey the king. The wicked are sometimes treated as the just deserve. No one can find out all that God does.
9: The same death comes to everyone. "Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might." The race is not to the swift.
10: Dead flies spoil perfume; a little folly outweighs wisdom. Sayings on rulers, laziness and careless speech.
Small faults can ruin much good.
11: Cast your bread on the waters
Be generous and take risks, for you do not know what will succeed. Young people should rejoice and remember that God will judge.
12: Remember God in your youth, before old age and death. The conclusion: "Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man."
The answer to the book's question lies beyond "under the sun".
